title: Content, padding, border, margin
learningObjectives: Explain content, padding, border, margin and use it in a practical layout.

understand.concept: The CSS box model describes content surrounded by padding, border, and margin. Content holds text or child content; padding adds space inside the border; border draws an edge; margin creates space outside the border. With content-box, padding and border add to the declared width.
understand.whyItMatters: Fixed dimensions can cause overflow when content grows. Understanding the layers helps estimate component size and diagnose unexpected gaps.
understand.analogy: Think of a parcel: content is the item, padding is protective packing, border is the box wall, and margin is the gap between parcels.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy supports intuition; browser layout follows the CSS formatting and sizing rules.

explain.narrative: Under content-box, the border-box width is 180 + 40 + 10 = 230 CSS pixels, excluding margins.

examples.explanation: Under content-box, the border-box width is 180 + 40 + 10 = 230 CSS pixels, excluding margins.

questions.prompt: Which box-model area creates space outside the border?
questions.explanation: Margin is the outer spacing area around the border box.
